questions.q: What is the purpose of identity resolution?
options: To encrypt customer emails before ingestion
To decide which records describe the same person or account and build a unified profile
To refresh data streams on a schedule
To build charts in Tableau Next
questions.explain: Identity resolution links records from different sources that belong to the same person or account and produces a unified profile.

questions.q: How do match rules behave within a ruleset?
options: Profiles match when all criteria within one rule are satisfied, and separate rules are combined with OR
Profiles match if any single criterion in any rule is true
Match rules only compare record IDs
Match rules run before any data is ingested
questions.explain: Each rule can contain several criteria that must all be met, and a record can match through any one of the rules in the ruleset.

options: Decide which source systems are allowed to connect
Delete the duplicate source records after matching
Choose a single value for a unified field when matched records disagree
Schedule the ruleset to run nightly
questions.explain: Reconciliation rules select one value, for example the most frequent or the one from a preferred source, when matched records hold different values.

questions.q: What happens to the original source records after identity resolution?
options: They are overwritten by the unified profile
They are permanently deleted
They are converted into segments
They remain in place; the unified profile is a new layer linked back to them
questions.explain: The unified profile is created alongside the source data, with links that let you trace it back to contributing records.

questions.q: A ruleset shows a unified count almost equal to the source count. What does that most likely suggest?
options: Very little consolidation happened, so the rules may be too strict
The rules are perfectly tuned
The data streams have stopped refreshing
Reconciliation rules were not configured
questions.explain: If almost nothing merged, duplicates probably remain. Review whether the match criteria are too strict, and check against real records.
